# Baritone dependency

Analyzer's optional automation integration uses the public `baritone.api` interface from the **unmodified official Baritone Fabric API 1.13.1 release**, targeting Minecraft Java 1.21.4. This is the API release, which also supplies the functioning pathfinder, rather than the standalone variant with stripped integration names. The dependency is installed as a separate Fabric mod; Analyzer does not shade or merge its classes into the Analyzer JAR.

Official references: [release 1.13.1](https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/releases/tag/v1.13.1), [installation and version table](https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/blob/1.21.4/SETUP.md), [public API documentation/source](https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/tree/v1.13.1/src/api/java/baritone/api), [source commit](https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/tree/a99e25eb8dc2f5b18229c74ba77ae9e5b682dbb3).

The official JAR is `baritone-api-fabric-1.13.1.jar`. Its SHA-256 is `bfb79c3cdb8fe1f7697999b1f9c7f08ea29775f3b69d48ad90c387690ee67b05`, verified against the [GitHub release API asset digest](https://api.github.com/repos/cabaletta/baritone/releases/tags/v1.13.1). Its SHA-1 is `7e2283bb1a1e9cff00ec0278a82568dc33ada382`, verified against the [official checksum file](https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/releases/download/v1.13.1/checksums.txt). `PROVENANCE.json` records both identities, source links and the locally calculated source archive hash. The JAR's own Fabric metadata specifies Minecraft 1.21.4 and mod ID `baritone`.

Baritone is copyright its upstream contributors and distributed under the LGPL version 3 or later. This directory preserves the official LGPL license, upstream `LICENSE-Part-2.jpg`, the GPL version 3 text incorporated by the LGPL, official checksums, and the complete corresponding official `v1.13.1` source archive. The source archive includes upstream build scripts and build instructions. Baritone has not been modified. Its separately replaceable JAR can be replaced with a compatible API build or removed from the mods folder. Analyzer's integration source remains available in the Analyzer source archive. Keep these notices and corresponding source with redistributions that contain this dependency.

The official Fabric JAR also contains the upstream `nether-pathfinder` native helper as a nested JAR. Analyzer does not directly invoke its API or claim the native helper as original code; upstream maintains it as part of this dependency. No Baritone implementation classes are used by Analyzer, and no upstream implementation source was copied into Analyzer.

## Integration behavior

`BaritoneBridge` lazily loads its typed adapter after checking Fabric's `baritone` mod ID. Analyzer can still load, render and edit mission plans when Baritone is absent. Dispatching travel, mining or building requires the official API mod and a living player in a world.

Travel uses public `GoalXZ` or `GoalBlock` goals. Mining uses `IMineProcess.mineByName`, with requested counts interpreted as the total matching inventory quantity. Completion is checked against observed player inventory using the public block/drop filter. A process becoming inactive without reaching the quantity is a failure, rather than a claimed success. Travel completion requires the player's actual block position to satisfy the goal. Shelter completion requires every schematic cell to match the actual loaded world.

Analyzer does not replace an already active manual Baritone task. While Analyzer owns a task, its pause control uses a temporary public `IBaritoneProcess` to request a safe pause. Cancel checks that the task still belongs to Analyzer and that another process has not taken over. Manual Baritone commands relinquish Analyzer's ownership. Analyzer does not write global Baritone settings or call `forceCancel`. External integrations issuing an identical mining command directly through the same public mine process cannot always be distinguished using Baritone's public API; ordinary chat commands and changed goals/processes are detected.

The original starter shelter is **7 x 7 x 5**, with a floor, walls, roof and two-block-high entrance. It requires **168 solid material blocks** on an empty site. Its schematic has no desired blocks outside the selected volume. The preflight rejects unloaded cells, fluids, block entities and unbreakable obstacles. Normal Baritone pathfinding still follows the user's own movement, break and placement settings; it can change terrain while finding routes. Choose a clear site with access around the shelter. Analyzer reports actual missing blocks and refuses a build with insufficient inventory material.

Baritone's `allowInventory` defaults to false. Tools and building material must therefore be available on the hotbar unless the user has enabled that setting themselves. Analyzer's task engine stages its mining tools and required shelter material through normal inventory swaps before dispatch; direct bridge calls still require hotbar supplies. Survival mining needs suitable tools, resources must exist, and protected blocks or server movement rules can prevent a route. The integration cannot guarantee escape from a particular public server's spawn region.
